newsitem.title: USA: Group eyes new lawsuit on Milwaukee stadium tax.
newsitem.headline: Group eyes new lawsuit on Milwaukee stadium tax.

text.p: A group of Milwaukee area taxpayers will file a new lawsuit to stop a partially bond-financed stadium for the Milwaukee Brewers American League baseball team, a member of the group said Friday.

George Watts said the group is in the process of seeking an attorney to file a lawsuit either in Racine or Milwaukee county circuit court to block issuance of $160 million of tax-exempt bonds for the project.
He said he believes the group has 30 days from the Nov. 15 approval of a bond resolution by the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District board to file a challenge to the bonds.

As for the grounds of the lawsuit, Watts said he believes there is some "vulnerability" in the bond documents that can be challenged. He added the aim of the lawsuit is to buy time for a U.S. Appeals Court in Chicago to hear an appeal of the group's constitutional challenge to a five-county, 0.1 percent sales tax the Wisconsin Legislature enacted to back the baseball park district's bond issue.
The group filed the appeal after the lawsuit was dismissed by a U.S. District Court judge in Milwaukee. A similar lawsuit filed by the group was also dismissed by the Wisconsin Supreme Court.

Watts said he hoped the new lawsuit would delay the sale of the bonds until the U.S. Appeals Court has time to rule or U.S. Sen. Patrick Moynihan can reintroduce his bill in January banning the use of tax-exempt bonds for professional sports stadiums.
The sale of the bonds for the Brewers ballpark has been tentatively set for the week before Christmas.
A spokesman for the baseball park district board said the board was aware of the possibility of a new lawsuit and was working with legal counsel to deal with it.

Jon Axelrod, a Madison attorney representing the board, was not available for comment. Axelrod has said that the constitutional challenge to the sales tax was without merit and that he would forward that opinion to bond counsel on the deal.

In addition to proceeds from the $160 million bond issue, the $250 million convertible-roofed stadium will be funded with $50 million in loans to the Brewers from the city of Milwaukee, the local business community and two foundations, and $40 million from the sale of naming rights to Miller Brewing Co., upfront concession payments and a letter of credit from the American League.
